limitation: Minimized cases derived from observed project failures and review noise; they prove only that the named historical conditions remain guarded. They are not a representative vulnerability benchmark or a production precision/recall measurement.

cases.title: The main risk summary rendered JavaScript objects
cases.observedFailure: A v3 report with risk-domain state totals rendered [object Object] in Markdown and HTML.
cases.protectedContract: Markdown and HTML risk summaries render numeric state and severity totals.
cases.remainingBoundary: Golden rendering tests protect the current fixture shapes; they do not prove every future presentation is understandable.

cases.title: A pnpm workspace could receive a false confirmed lockfile absence
cases.observedFailure: A root pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml covering apps/* still allowed a child package.json to be reported as confirmed missing-lockfile evidence.
cases.protectedContract: A covered pnpm package inherits its workspace lockfile; only proven uncovered manifests may be confirmed.
cases.remainingBoundary: The parser supports the documented bounded subset and is not a general YAML evaluator.

cases.title: Nested JS/TS templates could make a whole file partial
cases.observedFailure: A nested template such as const html = `${``}` produced unterminated_string_literal and stopped normal source-rule coverage for that file.
cases.protectedContract: Nested template literals do not silently remove normal JS/TS source-rule coverage.
cases.remainingBoundary: The tokenizer is still bounded and reports unsupported syntax as incomplete evidence rather than silently passing it.

cases.title: A path-only rename could make a retest exit successfully
cases.observedFailure: Renaming a file without removing its condition produced one fixed and one new finding, allowing the compatible baseline gate to exit successfully.
cases.protectedContract: A unique path-equivalent condition remains unresolved instead of becoming fixed plus new.
cases.remainingBoundary: condition_moved means an equivalent condition exists elsewhere; it does not prove historical identity or that a git move caused it.

cases.title: Numeric SVG innerHTML remains a review-visible expected match

source.note: Minimized from an external real-project review; original project content is not included.

cases.observedFailure: A numeric-only SVG string assembled with innerHTML matched the intentionally broad DOM-sink rule.
cases.protectedContract: Context-dependent DOM sinks stay visible for human closure and are not silently suppressed.

evidence.requiredClosure: Confirm that every interpolated value remains numeric and no untrusted markup reaches the sink.

cases.remainingBoundary: This fixture is benign only because its constructed values are numeric. The detector does not trace arbitrary input or prove other innerHTML assignments safe.
